title: Higher ozone and wetter soil shifts had less same-site support than dry shifts in four eastern US forest samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We measured observed exposure support for joint ozone and soil moisture shifts in a published forest injury panel. Four Northeast and North Central samples in 1994-2002 and 2003-2010 had 5,277 site-years at sites with at least three records. Adding 10 ppm-h W126 ozone and one soil moisture SD had same-site convex-hull support at 0.33-0.98 percent of records. Adding ozone and removing one moisture SD had support at 2.12-5.09 percent. All four dry-minus-wet gaps exceeded the central 95 percent range from 99 within-site random pairings that kept separate exposure values fixed. Smaller shifts and full-period records raised support. At least six visits retained three gap signs and gave one tie. Short histories alone gave low leave-one-record-out coverage. These are finite-panel geometric results, not injury effects or causal positivity tests. Selected sites, coarse exposure, rounded source data and empty areas inside hulls limit use. The package gives code, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval instructions. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Support for +10 ppm-h ozone and a wet or dry one-SD soil moisture shift. Bars show joint hull support. Horizontal marks show separate exposure range support. These are selected-panel counts, not injury effects.

citations.reason: Verified forest exposure panel; exact entry and bundle hashes are recorded.
Uncertain repeated annual injury interaction motivates a different exposure support audit.
Directional support method applied to a separate forest injury archive and a different exposure pair. No code or bird records reused.
